notes: TBox revision. The rule is the diet of snakes, held by every model ("snakes are carnivores" 1,396, "snakes are carnivorous" 865 in Dolma; Wikipedia: "All snakes are strictly carnivorous"), with no real exception: snake frugivory is anecdotal (fruit found in a spitting cobra and an Indian rock python, the latter carrying insect larvae), and egg-, snail-, insect- and worm-eaters all count as carnivorous. "Carnivorous" is used, not "carnivore", to avoid the order Carnivora. The three derived queries name snakes described since 2014 and state their membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops), with no prey or habitat hint; the third is an application (what the zoo should feed it), asked open so the options are not named, and its original answer is "animals" (any prey). Well-known snakes (boa constrictor, pythons) are not asked, since a model may store their diet by name. Achalinus snakes are thought to eat earthworms (2 Dolma co-occurrences), which is still carnivorous. The leftover edit.scope field was dropped. The negation is asked as "Is it true that snakes are not herbivorous?" instead of "Is it false that ...?". Conjunction side fact: every frog is an amphibian (true); disjunction side fact: every penguin is a mammal (false). Near unrelated: whether a snake is a reptile or an amphibian (reptile), another class fact untouched by the edit; its reference differs from the new answer. Paired with contraction biology-delete-0019 and the TBox expansion paired with this record.
